questions.explanation_incorrect: The nucleus is the solid core; dust and ion tails can extend outward from the coma.

questions.question: Which way does a comet’s ion tail generally point?
options: Always exactly opposite the direction of orbital motion
Always perpendicular to the solar wind
questions.explanation_correct: The solar wind carries ionized gas away from the Sun, creating a generally antisolar ion tail.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The solar wind shapes the ion tail to point generally away from the Sun, not necessarily behind the comet’s direction of motion.

questions.question: What usually produces a meteor shower on Earth?
options: Earth crosses the plane of Saturn’s rings
Earth passes through a stream of debris left along an object’s orbit
The Sun ejects a burst of visible-light photons
questions.answer: Earth passes through a stream of debris left along an object’s orbit
questions.explanation_correct: Meteor showers occur when Earth encounters streams of small particles, many left by comets or asteroids.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A lunar eclipse occurs when the Moon enters Earth’s shadow; the other events do not explain a meteor shower.

questions.question: What does a redshift of a spectral line mean?
options: Its observed frequency is higher than the reference frequency
Its observed wavelength is longer than its reference wavelength
Its observed wavelength is shorter than its reference wavelength
questions.answer: Its observed wavelength is longer than its reference wavelength
questions.explanation_correct: Redshift means a shift to longer wavelengths relative to a reference; several physical processes can produce it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: In vacuum, longer wavelengths correspond to lower frequencies; an unchanged or shorter wavelength is not a redshift.

questions.question: What does one light-year measure?
options: The distance light travels in vacuum in one year
The distance light travels in vacuum in one day
The average distance between Earth and the Sun
The time light takes to travel from the Sun to Earth
questions.answer: The distance light travels in vacuum in one year
questions.explanation_correct: A light-year is a unit of distance, defined by the distance light travels in vacuum in a year.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An astronomical unit is approximately Earth’s average distance from the Sun; neither a day’s light-travel distance nor a travel time is a light-year.

questions.question: Which geometric effect allows distances to nearby stars to be measured from their apparent position shift as Earth orbits?
questions.explanation_correct: Stellar parallax is the apparent change in a nearby star’s position relative to more distant background stars as the observer’s viewpoint changes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Redshift concerns wavelength, nutation is an axial wobble, and limb darkening describes a brightness pattern.

questions.question: How can spectroscopy help identify chemical elements in a star?
options: A star’s angular diameter gives its full chemical composition
All elements produce the same spectral lines
Elements have characteristic spectral absorption or emission lines
The period of a star’s pulsation identifies every element
questions.answer: Elements have characteristic spectral absorption or emission lines
questions.explanation_correct: Atomic transitions produce characteristic line wavelengths that astronomers can compare with observations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pulsation periods and angular size do not uniquely identify atmospheric elements; different elements have distinct spectral lines.

questions.question: In vacuum, what happens to the frequency of electromagnetic radiation when its wavelength becomes shorter?
options: It becomes independent of light speed
questions.explanation_correct: In vacuum, wavelength multiplied by frequency equals the speed of light, so a shorter wavelength corresponds to a higher frequency.
questions.explanation_incorrect: At fixed light speed, frequency cannot decrease or stay unchanged when wavelength decreases; wavelength and frequency remain related by c = λf.

questions.question: What optical element gathers and focuses light in a reflecting telescope?
questions.explanation_correct: A reflecting telescope uses a primary mirror to gather and focus light.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A primary objective lens gathers light in a refracting telescope; a grating disperses light and a detector records it.

questions.question: What does astronomical interferometry combine to improve angular resolution?
options: Only catalog positions of unrelated stars
The total masses of observed planets
Measurements of one mirror’s diameter alone
Signals from separated telescopes or antennas
questions.answer: Signals from separated telescopes or antennas
questions.explanation_correct: An interferometer combines signals from separated collectors, using their separation to obtain fine angular resolution.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Interferometry combines signals; catalog entries, masses and a mirror-diameter measurement alone are not an interferometric array.

questions.question: What happens to the wavelength of light traveling through an expanding universe?
options: It remains unchanged solely because the photon is moving
Its frequency rises while its wavelength increases
It is stretched toward longer wavelengths
It is compressed toward shorter wavelengths
questions.answer: It is stretched toward longer wavelengths
questions.explanation_correct: Cosmological expansion stretches wavelengths, producing cosmological redshift.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Expansion stretches light toward longer wavelengths; for light in vacuum, the corresponding frequency decreases.

questions.question: Between which two planets does the main asteroid belt lie?
questions.explanation_correct: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other planet pairs do not bracket the main asteroid belt.
